patients.label: Adult cochlear implant recipient (patient 1) with severe facial nerve stimulation, reimplanted with the Neuro Zti CI
attribution_limitations: The number of electrodes tested intraoperatively with stimulus MB differs: Methods say measurements were taken on five electrodes for patient 1, whereas Table 2 and the results text give FNS on 12 of 16 electrodes tested.
Authors state that stimulation artifact may have triggered the FN monitor alert for patient 1, so patient 1 intraoperative FN thresholds may not reflect myogenic responses.

Table 1 aetiology column names an aetiology without stating what it is the aetiology of; the Full Insertion (Yr) column of Table 2 does not state what the year refers to; the 1-yr cell of Table 2 prints 22% BKB FQ and 1.5 yrs without a space.

patients.label: Adult cochlear implant recipient (patient 2) with late-onset severe facial nerve stimulation, reimplanted with the Neuro Zti CI
attribution_limitations: Table 2 gives FNS with stimulus MB on 1/14 electrodes tested for patient 2, whereas the results text states 13 electrodes tested at a 25 μV monitor threshold with no FNS and a response on electrode 16 only when the threshold was reduced to 20 μV. Table 3 shows 13 intra-cochlear cells for patient 2.
The Table 3 patient 2 row label carries an asterisk while the footnote defining the reduced 20 μV monitor setting is marked (a); the text, not the marker, places the electrode 16 response at 20 μV.
The break is described as advised, suggested and given (Table 1: Yes, no improvement, 1 wk).

Table 1 aetiology column and the Table 2 Full Insertion (Yr) column do not state what the aetiology explains or what the year refers to; the post-reimplantation cell prints 7 wks as a single follow-up.
Insertion depth of the Neuro Zti relative to the original CI22 M is stated as the same depth in the results but as marginally shallower in the discussion.

patients.label: Adult cochlear implant recipient (patient 3) with severe facial nerve stimulation since switch-on, reimplanted with the Neuro Zti CI
attribution_limitations: Table 1 aetiology column does not state what the aetiology explains, and the possible dehiscence structure is not named. Speech testing is reported at 4 mo in Table 2 while the text gives 3-months postactivation for the functional report and a 2-mo loudness visit; these are different time points.

FIG. 1
Schematic of pulse shapes.
A, Patient 1: FN thresholds where stimulating levels were reported to have a “soft” loudness level.
B, Patient 2: FN thresholds where stimulating levels were reported to have “moderate-loud” loudness level.
C, Patient 3: FN thresholds where stimulating levels were reported to have “soft” loudness level.

limitations: Three supplementary DOCX files (supplementary tables 1 and 2, supplementary figures 1 and 2 are cited in the text) are listed as figures s001 to s003 with no caption and no resolved URL, and the source declares no supplements; their content was not reviewed.

Cohort-level statements without an explicit all-patient wording (for example activation 2 to 6 weeks after surgery, electrode position confirmed by postoperative X-ray, programming limited loudness) are not copied to individual patients.
Values printed inside Figure 2 are pixel content recorded only in visual.json; no estimated plot values are recorded.
Patient sex and exact ages are not stated; the series reports adults only.
Discussion of a single control sample reimplanted with the same device cites supplementary table 2 and is not a patient of this series.
The Methods count of five electrodes tested for patient 1 conflicts with 12 of 16 in Table 2; patient 2 has 13 versus 14 electrodes tested.

Discussion sentence "All patients achieved adequate volume percept without FNS for stimulus MMA" is a study-level conclusion and is not copied; it is not treated as a conflict with patient 1 reaching only "medium" loudness on single-electrode testing, because "adequate" is not a loudness rating and MCL was reached for all active electrodes in routine programming.

Discussion sentence "none of the presented patients have experienced FNS since reimplantation" refers to clinical use; patient 1 and 3 FNS with stimulus MB during postoperative loudness testing is recorded per patient and the cohort sentence is not copied.
The Table 2 "Full Insertion (Yr)" years are not attached to the reimplant events because the header does not state which event the year dates.

Supplement acquisition (op2 dense supplement_assets acquire) found no declared supplements: the three DOCX files (s001 to s003) are parsed as figures, so no supplement manifest or supplement review exists.

Patient sex and exact ages are not stated; the series reports adults only.
Discussion of a single control sample reimplanted with the same device cites supplementary table 2 and is not a patient of this series.
The Methods count of five electrodes tested for patient 1 conflicts with 12 of 16 in Table 2; patient 2 has 13 versus 14 electrodes tested.

Discussion sentence "All patients achieved adequate volume percept without FNS for stimulus MMA" is a study-level conclusion and is not copied; it is not treated as a conflict with patient 1 reaching only "medium" loudness on single-electrode testing, because "adequate" is not a loudness rating and MCL was reached for all active electrodes in routine programming.

Discussion sentence "none of the presented patients have experienced FNS since reimplantation" refers to clinical use; patient 1 and 3 FNS with stimulus MB during postoperative loudness testing is recorded per patient and the cohort sentence is not copied.
The Table 2 "Full Insertion (Yr)" years are not attached to the reimplant events because the header does not state which event the year dates.

Supplement acquisition (op2 dense supplement_assets acquire) found no declared supplements: the three DOCX files (s001 to s003) are parsed as figures, so no supplement manifest or supplement review exists.

attribution_limitations: Table 2 gives FNS with stimulus MB on 1/14 electrodes tested for patient 2, whereas the results text states 13 electrodes tested at a 25 μV monitor threshold with no FNS and a response on electrode 16 only when the threshold was reduced to 20 μV. Table 3 shows 13 intra-cochlear cells for patient 2.
The Table 3 patient 2 row label carries an asterisk while the footnote defining the reduced 20 μV monitor setting is marked (a); the text, not the marker, places the electrode 16 response at 20 μV.
The break is described as advised, suggested and given (Table 1: Yes, no improvement, 1 wk).

Table 1 aetiology column and the Table 2 Full Insertion (Yr) column do not state what the aetiology explains or what the year refers to; the post-reimplantation cell prints 7 wks as a single follow-up.
Insertion depth of the Neuro Zti relative to the original CI22 M is stated as the same depth in the results but as marginally shallower in the discussion.

claims.text: An adult cochlear implant recipient with meningitis as the listed aetiology was implanted with a Cochlear CI22 M in 1995. FNS developed after 13 years of CI use and progressed, with speech recognition deteriorating. Grounding configuration changes altered current requirements but FNS remained problematic in all conditions, and a one-week break did not change the FN threshold or loudness.

claims.text: Reimplantation with the Neuro Zti device was offered and the patient was reimplanted with the Neuro Zti EVO electrode by a round window approach, leaving seven extra-cochlear electrodes. Intraoperative testing showed an FN response with stimulus MB on one electrode and none with stimulus MMA. Ten of 20 electrodes were later deactivated, seven extra-cochlear at surgery and three apparently extruded.

limitations: Three supplementary DOCX files (supplementary tables 1 and 2, supplementary figures 1 and 2 are cited in the text) are listed as figures s001 to s003 with no caption and no resolved URL, and the source declares no supplements; their content was not reviewed.

Cohort-level statements without an explicit all-patient wording (for example activation 2 to 6 weeks after surgery, electrode position confirmed by postoperative X-ray, programming limited loudness) are not copied to individual patients.
Values printed inside Figure 2 are pixel content recorded only in visual.json; no estimated plot values are recorded.
Patient sex and exact ages are not stated; the series reports adults only.
Discussion of a single control sample reimplanted with the same device cites supplementary table 2 and is not a patient of this series.
The Methods count of five electrodes tested for patient 1 conflicts with 12 of 16 in Table 2; patient 2 has 13 versus 14 electrodes tested.

Discussion sentence "All patients achieved adequate volume percept without FNS for stimulus MMA" is a study-level conclusion and is not copied; it is not treated as a conflict with patient 1 reaching only "medium" loudness on single-electrode testing, because "adequate" is not a loudness rating and MCL was reached for all active electrodes in routine programming.

Discussion sentence "none of the presented patients have experienced FNS since reimplantation" refers to clinical use; patient 1 and 3 FNS with stimulus MB during postoperative loudness testing is recorded per patient and the cohort sentence is not copied.
The Table 2 "Full Insertion (Yr)" years are not attached to the reimplant events because the header does not state which event the year dates.

Supplement acquisition (op2 dense supplement_assets acquire) found no declared supplements: the three DOCX files (s001 to s003) are parsed as figures, so no supplement manifest or supplement review exists.

Despite stimulation level differences, changing grounding configuration did not improve auditory function or reduce FNS in any condition.
Before developing FNS, patients 1 and 2 achieved >90% on BKB sentences.
In clinical use, all patients reported reduced FNS and showed an improvement in Bamford-Kowal-Bench sentences recognition compared with immediately before reimplantation.
All patients reported a subjective improvement in communication with the new implant, and could follow conversation in a quiet room, without lip reading, and with minimal repetition.
Patients 1 and 2 had difficulty adapting to the new sound after long-term CI use, but continue to report acclimatization over time.

Patient 2 showed similar BKB outcomes with a female speaker compared with their previous implant when they still had auditory benefit, but BKB scores with the male speaker were lower with the new device.
their best functional outcomes were measured with their original implants before the onset of FNS
Before developing FNS, patients 1 and 2 achieved >90% on BKB sentences. Although function with the new device has gradually improved, performance remains 40-percentage point below their best scores.
Bamford-Kowal-Bench scores with a male speaker were lower compared with measurements taken before the onset of severe FNS for patients 1 and 2.
Minimal changes were required during the first 2 months for all patients.
Three adult CI recipients with severe FNS were offered a replacement implant when standard stimulation strategies and programming adjustments did not resolve symptoms.

claims.text: An adult cochlear implant recipient with ototoxicity and possible dehiscence listed as aetiology was implanted with a MED-EL Synchrony Flex28 in August 2019. FNS occurred on activation, no break was given, and biphasic and triphasic stimulation with monopolar grounding did not improve FNS or hearing. The patient was never able to understand speech with the CI alone.

limitations: Three supplementary DOCX files (supplementary tables 1 and 2, supplementary figures 1 and 2 are cited in the text) are listed as figures s001 to s003 with no caption and no resolved URL, and the source declares no supplements; their content was not reviewed.

Cohort-level statements without an explicit all-patient wording (for example activation 2 to 6 weeks after surgery, electrode position confirmed by postoperative X-ray, programming limited loudness) are not copied to individual patients.
Values printed inside Figure 2 are pixel content recorded only in visual.json; no estimated plot values are recorded.
Patient sex and exact ages are not stated; the series reports adults only.
Discussion of a single control sample reimplanted with the same device cites supplementary table 2 and is not a patient of this series.
The Methods count of five electrodes tested for patient 1 conflicts with 12 of 16 in Table 2; patient 2 has 13 versus 14 electrodes tested.

Discussion sentence "All patients achieved adequate volume percept without FNS for stimulus MMA" is a study-level conclusion and is not copied; it is not treated as a conflict with patient 1 reaching only "medium" loudness on single-electrode testing, because "adequate" is not a loudness rating and MCL was reached for all active electrodes in routine programming.

Discussion sentence "none of the presented patients have experienced FNS since reimplantation" refers to clinical use; patient 1 and 3 FNS with stimulus MB during postoperative loudness testing is recorded per patient and the cohort sentence is not copied.
The Table 2 "Full Insertion (Yr)" years are not attached to the reimplant events because the header does not state which event the year dates.

Supplement acquisition (op2 dense supplement_assets acquire) found no declared supplements: the three DOCX files (s001 to s003) are parsed as figures, so no supplement manifest or supplement review exists.
